header:
Date: 2027-03-19 | Start: 13:30 PT | Duration: 48 minutes
Redwood: Avery Chen (AE), Marcus Doyle (SE) | NorthCrest: Linda Park (VP Eng), Jamal Ortiz (Head of Data), Priya Menon (Sec&Compliance)
transcript:
[00:00] Avery: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Avery from Redwood Inference. We've got Marcus with me, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Linda: Doing well, thanks. Hi Avery, hi Marcus.
[00:09] Jamal: Hey all, Jamal here. Excited to get this kicked off.
[00:12] Priya: Hi, Priya on SecOps side, I'll jump in on compliance stuff.
[00:16] Marcus: Quick agenda — run through the onboarding playbook, talk SSO and network access, billing models, and finish with next steps & pilot plan. Sound good?
[00:24] Linda: Yep. We're specifically trying to validate latency & cost for our customer service workflows and lock in SSO for our agents.
[00:30] Jamal: Also we have to tee up approvals for the pilot from infra — latency targets are sub-300ms ideally for short prompts, and cost targets per 1k tokens is a gating metric.
[00:40] Avery: Great, we can work to meet that. One note up front: we recommend starting on hosted for speed, then move to dedicated when throughput and predictability is required, and private for the highest compliance needs. We'll walk through numbers.
[00:55] [00:55] Marcus: To be pragmatic, we usually provision a staging host in the customer's preferred region and run a quick perf harness — about 2-3 hours of synthetic load plus a few real prompt sets. That gives a ballpark for latency and token cost.
[01:12] Linda: For SSO, our security team requires SAML 2.0 with role mapping to our Okta groups. We also need an audit trail for who called what model and a per-route cost breakdown for chargebacks.
[01:26] Priya: And SOC2 reports — we need to see scope for logging, key management (KMS/HSM), and whether Redwood stores any request bodies in logs.
[01:36] Marcus: Quick clarifying note — logs are retained by default for X days in hosted; for dedicated/private we can configure retention and ensure PII redaction. Sorry if that number's fuzzy, I'll reconfirm the retention windows in writing.
[01:50] Jamal: Okay, good. On networking — we prefer VPC peering or PrivateLink type connectivity, not opening public endpoints. Is that supported for dedicated?
[01:59] Avery: Yes, dedicated and private both support VPC peering and private networking. For hosted we have an egress/IP allowlist option but it's not as isolated as VPC.
[02:09] Linda: Billing — we need to understand committed monthly spend vs pay-as-you-go. If we commit to dedicated, what's the break-even for cost and how would billing look?
[02:19] Marcus: We have a simple model: hosted is per-token usage, dedicated is a monthly reserved capacity with lower per-token effective cost and guaranteed throughput. We also offer burst credits and autoscale policies. I'll attach a spreadsheet with scenarios.
[02:33] [02:33] Speaker 1: Uh, sorry my mic just faded — back now.
[02:37] Avery: No problem. I'll cover the high-level playbook now. Step one: kickoff (this call), step two: staging access & SSO wiring, step three: pilot (2 weeks), step four: evaluation and decide lift to dedicated/private, and step five: production ramp.
[02:55] Jamal: For pilot success criteria — we want: average p95 latency <350ms, cost per 1k tokens under $2.5 (example), and parity of answers compared to our control model in 90% of sanity evaluations.
[03:12] Marcus: Nice, we can instrument those. We'll run a regression suite over your prompt set and give quality metrics as part of the pilot output.
[03:20] Priya: On encryption — does Redwood support Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) or Cloud KMS? Our policy prefers BYOK for production.
[03:28] Marcus: For private deployments we can support customer-managed keys (BYOK). For hosted, we integrate with cloud KMS and offer envelope encryption; again I'll confirm specifics for your cloud.
[03:37] Avery: Two quick commercialization notes — if NorthCrest expects to keep data inside bank boundaries we recommend the private package; if you want lower friction and faster time-to-value, hosted or dedicated can bridge that gap.
[03:50] Linda: Our legal team will want the data flow diagram and a strawman DPA. Can you send those?
[03:56] Avery: Yes, DPA and data flow diagram — we'll include them with the security pack.
[04:00] [04:00] Jamal: About quality regressions — we need to lock a prompt set that we run automatically every day, and alerts if response quality drops. Does Redwood have built-in evals?
[04:09] Marcus: Yes, Redwood Optimize includes eval monitoring tied to prompt sets and regression alerts. For pilot we'll set up a baseline and tie alerts to Slack/email.
[04:18] Priya: Do you log raw prompt/response pairs? Our compliance constraints may require redaction, and in some cases we will only send hashed prompts.
[04:26] Marcus: We can redact or hash at the edge — you can also run a pre-processor to strip PHI. I'll add an option in the runbook.
[04:34] Linda: For SSO mapping — our agents use two Okta groups: "agents-tier1" and "agents-tier2". We need API roles for rate-limiting and per-role quotas.
[04:45] Marcus: Role mapping is supported; rate limits per token key and per-role quotas are configurable. We'll include an example SAML assertion mapping in the SSO notes.
[04:55] [04:55] Avery: Quick pause — any blockers to start the staging pilot this week?
[05:00] Jamal: Infra approvals are pending but we can greenlight once we get the runbook and the staging endpoint details.
[05:06] Priya: Security wants to pre-approve network egress policy and see the KMS plan.
[05:11] Avery: Understood. Marcus will share the runbook and a staging checklist with IP ranges and perf harness steps.
[05:18] Marcus: I'll include a small benchmark harness and a sample curl script — also a note on KV cache behaviors for chat state. Heads-up, transcription might say "K-V cash" in some docs, that's just our Vocab issue in automatic notes.
[05:32] Linda: Ha, noted.
[05:35] Marcus: Also we'll collect token breakdowns per route so you can cost-allocate to teams.
[05:41] Jamal: On model choice — are you recommending a quantized medium model or surfaced larger family? We need balance between cost and hallucination risk.
[05:50] Marcus: We'll recommend model variants: smaller quantized models for high-volume templated responses; larger models for open-ended tasks. For pilot we can run two variants and report both cost and a small evaluation on quality delta.
[06:05] Priya: Another compliance item — we need to know where logs/metrics are stored and retention windows.
[06:11] Marcus: Hosted defaults to 30 days of request logs; dedicated/private you control retention. All logging endpoints can be exported to your SIEM (Splunk/Datadog) via secure forwarders.
[06:23] Linda: Ok, let's talk timeline — if we start onboarding this week, how long until we have staging perf data?
[06:30] Marcus: Usually 3-5 business days: SSO wiring (1-2 days), provisioning staging endpoint (same day once details are in), benchmark run and report (1-2 days). So worst case a week.
[06:44] Avery: And billing — to help decisions we will send three scenarios: pure hosted, monthly dedicated reservation, and private (license + infra). Each will include estimated 1k-token cost, reserved throughput, and minimum commitment.
[06:59] Jamal: Will the dedicated plan have an SLA for p99 latency? We need guarantees for peak windows.
[07:05] Marcus: Yes, dedicated tiers have SLA targets and compensation clauses; exact p99 numbers vary by region/hardware, we'll add those to the pricing doc.
[07:14] [07:14] Speaker 2: There's a brief crosstalk, hold on.
[07:18] Priya: Also, does Redwood offer pen tests or third-party attestation for private installs?
[07:22] Avery: We can coordinate a pen test for private deployments; we have partner certs and can provide SOC2 Type II reports for hosted as part of the security pack.
[07:31] Linda: For the pilot, our success criteria will be the three Jamal listed plus SSO working for two sample users and logs forwarded to our Splunk sandbox.
[07:41] Marcus: We'll set up a test plan doc — steps for SSO, steps for benchmark and the exact prompt set to run.
[07:48] Jamal: One more on billing — are there tooling credits or onboarding discounts? If we commit to a quarter, that affects our internal chargeback.
[07:56] Avery: We do have onboarding credits and multi-month discounts for committed DALs. Pricing sheet will call them out.
[08:03] [08:03] Marcus: I'll also include an example of model rollouts — canary, A/B, automatic fallback to lighter models if capacity constrained. That might help operations.
[08:14] Linda: Good. Security wants an architecture diagram showing what data leaves our VPC and what stays on-prem. Do you have a template?
[08:21] Avery: Yes, we'll provide a data flow diagram template and a filled example for the pilot.
[08:25] Priya: For the DPA, can you show where responsibility lies for data deletion requests? We need a clause for 48-hour response to deletion requests.
[08:33] Avery: We can support that — we'll flag timeframes in the DPA.
[08:36] [08:36] Jamal: Ok, should we read back next steps so nothing falls through?
[08:40] Avery: Sure. I'll share the pricing scenarios and DPA/security pack by Tuesday 3/22. Marcus will provide the runbook, staging checklist, and perf harness by Monday 3/21. Priya will confirm audit artifact list and deletion policy by 3/24.
[08:57] Linda: That works. We'll aim to approve infra for pilot once we get the runbook.
[09:02] Marcus: One final note — during the pilot we'll enable token-level breakdowns and a small sampling of responses for quality review; we'll redact PII per request.
[09:12] Priya: Please add the redaction options to the runbook.
[09:15] Avery: Will do. Any other questions?
[09:18] Linda: No, thanks. This helped clarify.
[09:21] Jamal: Good session.
[09:22] Priya: Thanks, talk soon.
[09:24] Avery: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the doc pack and the pricing.
[09:28] [09:28] END OF RECORDING (48 minutes approx)

Notes on transcript: automated speaker labeling may have minor errors and occasional homophone substitutions (e.g., "KV cache" transcribed as "K-V cash"). Some filler words and overlaps retained to reflect natural call cadence.
file_notes: Staging endpoint requested: region us-east-1. Pilot length agreed: 2 weeks. Primary eval set will be 500 prompts supplied by NorthCrest. Billing scenarios to include 3, 6, 12 month commitments.
